nodes.summary: `P₁(A) = ∫_A f₁`.
nodes.title: Non-null law as the integral of the non-null density

nodes.summary: The law `P₁` of a non-null z-value.
nodes.title: Law of a non-null z-value

nodes.summary: Efron et al. (2001): `fdr(Z) = P(H = 0 | Z)` almost surely, as a conditional expectation of the null indicator given the z-value.
nodes.title: Local fdr is the posterior null probability

nodes.summary: `P(H = 0 | Z ∈ Γ) = Fdr(Γ)`: the tail-area false discovery rate is the posterior null probability given `Z ∈ Γ` (Storey 2002, Theorem 1; Efron 2010, ch. 2). Both sides are `0` when `P(Z ∈ Γ) = 0`.
nodes.title: Tail-area fdr is the posterior null probability given a region

nodes.summary: The mixture density is integrable.
nodes.title: Mixture density is integrable
Joint probability of a non-null case in a set

nodes.summary: Efron et al. (2001): `P(H = 0, Z ∈ A) = ∫_A fdr(z) dP_Z(z)` for every measurable `A`, so `fdr(Z)` is a version of the posterior null probability `P(H = 0 | Z)`.
nodes.title: Null probability as an integral of the local fdr

nodes.summary: `P(H = 0, Z ∈ A) = π₀ P₀(A)`.
nodes.title: Joint probability of a null case in a set

nodes.summary: The z-value has the mixture law: `P(Z ∈ A) = ∫_A f`.
nodes.title: z-value has the mixture law

nodes.summary: Joint law of (null indicator, z-value) on `Bool × ℝ`; `true` means the case is null.
nodes.title: Joint law of null indicator and z-value

nodes.summary: Conservative bias of Storey's (2002) estimator for a fixed set `H0` of true nulls: if their p-values are valid, then `E[π̂₀(t)] ≥ m₀ / m` for every `t ∈ [0, 1)`. No independence is assumed; the non-null p-values are arbitrary measurable functions.
nodes.title: Conservative bias of Storey's null proportion estimator

nodes.summary: The local false discovery rate is at most one.
nodes.title: Local false discovery rate is at most one

nodes.summary: The basic identity `fdr(z) f(z) = π₀ f₀(z)`, for every `z` (where `f(z) = 0` both sides vanish because `π₀ f₀ ≤ f`).
nodes.title: Local fdr times mixture density equals the null part

nodes.summary: The local false discovery rate is nonnegative.
nodes.title: Local false discovery rate is nonnegative

nodes.summary: Efron's local false discovery rate `fdr(z) = π₀ f₀(z) / f(z)` (zero where `f(z) = 0`).
nodes.title: Local false discovery rate

nodes.summary: The law of the z-value under the joint law is the mixture `f · Lebesgue`.
nodes.title: Marginal z-value law of the joint law is the mixture

nodes.summary: The local false discovery rate is measurable.
nodes.title: Local false discovery rate is measurable

nodes.summary: The mixture density is measurable.
nodes.title: Mixture density is measurable

nodes.summary: The mixture density is nonnegative.
nodes.title: Mixture density is nonnegative

nodes.summary: The mixture density `f = π₀ f₀ + (1 - π₀) f₁` of the z-values.
nodes.title: Mixture density of the two-groups model

nodes.summary: The q-value is monotone in the statistic.
nodes.title: q-value is monotone in the statistic

nodes.summary: The null part of the mixture is dominated by the mixture: `π₀ f₀ ≤ f`.
nodes.title: Null part of the mixture is dominated by the mixture

nodes.summary: `P₀(A) = ∫_A f₀`.
nodes.title: Null law as the integral of the null density

nodes.summary: The law `P₀` of a null z-value.
nodes.title: Law of a null z-value

nodes.summary: The true-null set of an outcome vector `x : Fin m → Bool × Bool`, where `(x i).1` records that hypothesis `i` is null and `(x i).2` that it is rejected.
nodes.title: True-null set of a test outcome vector

nodes.summary: The probability `∏ᵢ q(xᵢ)` of an outcome vector when the `m` (null, rejected) pairs are i.i.d. with law `q`.
nodes.title: Probability of a test outcome vector

nodes.summary: The law of one test's (null, rejected) pair in the two-groups model when the test rejects iff its z-value lies in `Γ`.
nodes.title: Law of a test's null and rejection pair

nodes.summary: Storey (2002), Theorem 1: for `m ≥ 1` i.i.d. tests, `pFDR = P(H = 0 | T ∈ Γ)`, where `q (true, true) = P(H = 0, T ∈ Γ)` and `q (false, true) = P(H = 1, T ∈ Γ)`. The identity is homogeneous in `q`, so only `q ≥ 0` is assumed; when `P(T ∈ Γ) = 0` both sides are `0`.
nodes.title: Storey's theorem: pFDR is a posterior null probability

nodes.summary: Storey (2002), Theorem 1, in the two-groups model: for `m ≥ 1` i.i.d. tests rejecting on `Γ`, `pFDR(Γ) = π₀ P₀(Γ) / P(Γ) = Fdr(Γ)`.
nodes.title: Storey's theorem in the two-groups model

nodes.summary: Storey's positive false discovery rate `pFDR = E[V / R | R > 0]` for `m` tests whose (null, rejected) indicator pairs are i.i.d. with law `q`: `V / R` is the false discovery proportion.
nodes.title: Storey's positive false discovery rate

nodes.summary: When the pFDR is nondecreasing along the nested regions, the q-value is the pFDR.
nodes.title: q-value equals the pFDR when the pFDR is monotone

nodes.summary: The q-value is at most the pFDR of the smallest region containing the statistic.
nodes.title: q-value is at most the pFDR of the smallest region

nodes.summary: Storey's (2003) q-value for a nested family of rejection regions `Γ_s = {T ≤ s}` with `pFDR(Γ_s) = pfdr s`: `q(t) = inf_{s ≥ t} pfdr s`, the smallest pFDR over the regions that contain the observed statistic `t`.
nodes.title: Storey's q-value

nodes.summary: The rejection set of an outcome vector.
nodes.title: Rejection set of a test outcome vector

nodes.summary: Storey's estimator `π̂₀(t) = #{i | pᵢ > t} / (m (1 - t))` of the proportion of true nulls, for a tuning parameter `t ∈ [0, 1)`.
nodes.title: Storey's estimator of the null proportion

nodes.summary: `E[fdr(Z) | Z ∈ Γ] = Fdr(Γ)`, written with densities: the tail-area false discovery rate is the `f`-weighted average of the local false discovery rate over `Γ` (Efron 2010, ch. 5).
nodes.title: Tail-area fdr is the average local fdr over the region

nodes.summary: The tail-area false discovery rate of a region `Γ`: `Fdr(Γ) = π₀ P₀(Γ) / P(Γ)`, written with the densities. Efron's `Fdr(z)` is `tailFdr (Set.Iic z)`. It is `0` when `P(Γ) = 0`.
nodes.title: Tail-area false discovery rate

nodes.summary: The two-groups model of Efron et al. (2001): prior null probability `π₀ ∈ [0, 1]`, null density `f₀` and non-null density `f₁` of the z-value (probability densities on `ℝ`).
nodes.title: Two-groups model

can_prove.label: ready to prove
can_prove.meaning: Statement is in Lean and nothing it needs is blocked, so the proof can start.

can_state.label: ready to state
can_state.meaning: Everything its statement uses is in Lean, so the statement can be written in Lean.

conditional.label: conditionally proved
conditional.meaning: Proof compiles, but rests on an open statement without a recorded Lean proof.

fully_proved.label: fully proved
fully_proved.meaning: Proved, and every prerequisite is fully proved too.

inventory_checked.label: inventory checked
inventory_checked.meaning: Module inventory checked in full; it records inspection, not a mathematical proof.

inventory_pending.label: inventory pending
inventory_pending.meaning: Module inventory not yet checked in full; it records inspection, not a mathematical proof.

not_ready.label: not ready
not_ready.meaning: Needs more blueprint work before it can be attempted.

proved.label: proved
proved.meaning: Proof compiles, but something it rests on is not finished.

stated.label: statement formalized
stated.meaning: Statement is in Lean; the proof is not.
